summary: Applying a blessed touchstone reaches apply.c:use_stone, which asks for a rubbing target and identifies an unknown gem. JavaScript doapply lacks the TOUCHSTONE/graystone arm and refuses at the selection prompt. Port complete use_stone and pure touchstone_ok through doapply and the graystone branch of dorub; the queue’s doapply label is the dispatcher, not the missing source function.

source.branch: A selected touchstone or other gray stone calls use_stone; a blessed touchstone rubbed with an unknown gem enters the identification branch, calls makeknown on stone and gem, and prints the renamed gem. The full function also handles known-target filtering, cursed shattering, self-rub, blind/hallucinating feedback, material streak/scratch effects, and command result timing.
callers: C apply.c:doapply dispatches FLINT, LUCKSTONE, LOADSTONE, and TOUCHSTONE to use_stone; JS js/apply.js:doapply refuses this arm.
C apply.c:dorub enters use_stone for a selected gray stone; JS js/apply.js:dorub currently throws for the graystone branch.
dependencies: C use_stone consumes getobj callback touchstone_ok; it is pure and needs source-pinned tests. Existing js/apply.js getobj supports callback predicates.
The cursed gem branch consumes bury.c:obj_resists, already present in js/bury.js; discovery uses hack.h makeknown (discover_object) and the final identified object line uses invent.c:prinv.
Source material/class helpers is_graystone, is_flimsy, object type/material/color tables, and pline/You/You_see messaging must preserve branch and output order.

evidence: Current saved challenges/evaluations/20260927142534-v8.json leaves 2 of 41 screens unmatched. Fresh scan at 56955495745cc647070474dbb74a558d5dfc2a24 stops at segment 0 step 39 after selecting the touchstone: JS raises UnsupportedApplyError for doapply object type 472; C waits for a second object.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:use_stone around lines 2680-2808 calls getobj, then identifies a gem when a blessed touchstone is rubbed against it; doapply around line 4397 calls use_stone for four graystone types. dorub around line 1798 is its other active caller. js/apply.js:doapply has no matching arm, and dorub explicitly refuses gray stones.
The source family is apply.c touchstone_ok/use_stone, not a generic doapply change or a rule based on the recorded seed, object letter, or ruby name.
